presentingComplaint: Progressive low back pain, fatigue and reduced urine output over 8 weeks
history: 68-year-old man with 2 months of worsening axial (thoracolumbar) bone pain, worse on movement, with intermittent rib pain after a minor cough. Increasing fatigue, exertional breathlessness and poor appetite with about 6 kg unintentional weight loss. Recent constipation, polyuria and low-grade confusion by family report. No fever, night sweats or trauma. PMH: hypertension. No known renal disease. Non-smoker.
examination: Pale, mildly dehydrated, alert but slowed. Tenderness over lower thoracic/lumbar spine and left lower ribs. No focal long-tract signs, no lymphadenopathy, no hepatosplenomegaly. Chest clear, no organomegaly. No rash, no joint swelling. Pertinent negatives: no fever, no meningism, no focal neuro deficit, no petechiae.
imaging: Whole-body low-dose CT / skeletal survey: multiple well-defined lytic 'punched-out' lesions in skull, vertebrae and ribs; a lytic lesion in T9 with mild vertebral height loss; no aggressive periosteal reaction. MRI spine confirms marrow infiltration without cord compression.
differentialDiagnoses: Metastatic carcinoma (e.g., prostate/lung) with lytic bone disease
Hypercalcaemia of malignancy from solid tumour
MGUS / smouldering myeloma (excluded by CRAB features)
finalDiagnosis: Multiple myeloma (symptomatic, with CRAB: hypercalcaemia, renal impairment, anaemia, lytic bone lesions)
citations: IMWG Diagnosis and Management of Multiple Myeloma 2014/updated criteria
contraindications: Avoid nephrotoxins and IV iodinated contrast where possible given AKI; hold NSAIDs
Bisphosphonate/zoledronic acid dose-adjust or avoid in significant renal impairment; ensure dental review before antiresorptives
Avoid gadolinium caution / correct hypercalcaemia and volume before any contrast
edgeCases: Non-secretory or light-chain-only myeloma can have a normal SPEP — serum free light chains and urine Bence Jones are essential
Cast nephropathy may present as the dominant feature (myeloma kidney) before bone pain
Hypercalcaemia can precipitate altered sensorium mimicking primary metabolic encephalopathy
expectedMaiK: Classic CRAB tetrad (hyperCalcaemia, Renal impairment, Anaemia, Bone lytic lesions) with a monoclonal protein points strongly to symptomatic multiple myeloma; confirm with SPEP/SFLC, urine light chains and bone marrow, and correct hypercalcaemia urgently.
expectedNextQuestions: Any prior monoclonal gammopathy (MGUS) or abnormal protein noted before?
Symptoms of cord compression — leg weakness, sphincter disturbance, saddle anaesthesia?
Any recurrent infections or bleeding suggesting marrow failure?
expectedInvestigations: Serum & urine protein electrophoresis with immunofixation and serum free light chain assay
Bone marrow aspirate/trephine with plasma cell % and cytogenetics (FISH)
Whole-body MRI or low-dose CT for bone disease staging; corrected calcium and renal function

investigations: Serum/urine protein electrophoresis with immunofixation and serum free light chains
Bone marrow biopsy with FISH cytogenetics
Skeletal survey / whole-body low-dose CT and corrected calcium

regressionAssertions: findings must include hypercalcemia and renalImpairment (CRAB features)
